title: Visibility and Encapsulation
learning_outcomes: Explain what visibility and encapsulation contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: public.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. In this lesson, focus on public; then compare it with protected. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use visibility and encapsulation when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. For visibility and encapsulation, begin with public. Also distinguish protected; private; encapsulating internal state. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Visibility and Encapsulation
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$json = "{\"items\":[1,2,3]}";
$payload = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
echo count($payload["items"]) . " items" . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
